overview: Trinidad and Tobago is an island country in the southern Caribbean, just off the coast of Venezuela. Its capital, Port of Spain, is on Trinidad. It became independent from the United Kingdom in 1962. Unlike most Caribbean countries, its economy is built mainly on oil and natural gas. It is the birthplace of the steelpan and calypso music, and its Carnival is world-famous.

geography.text: Trinidad, the larger island, has a range of hills in the north, plains in the centre and south, and swamps along parts of its coast. It is home to the Pitch Lake, the largest natural deposit of asphalt in the world. Tobago, to the north-east, is smaller and hillier, with coral reefs and beaches.

history.text: Trinidad was Spanish until Britain captured it in 1797, while Tobago changed hands many times. After slavery ended, workers came from India, and today the country blends African, Indian and other cultures. Trinidad and Tobago became independent in 1962, and oil and gas built its economy.

events.title: Columbus arrives
events.text: Columbus reaches Trinidad on his third voyage.

events.title: Workers from India
events.text: Indentured workers begin arriving from India.

government.text: Trinidad and Tobago is a parliamentary republic. The President, elected by parliament, is head of state, and the Prime Minister leads the government. Tobago has its own House of Assembly.

economy.text: Trinidad and Tobago is one of the richest countries in the Caribbean thanks to oil and natural gas. It is a major exporter of liquefied natural gas, ammonia and methanol. Pitch Lake in Trinidad is the world's largest natural deposit of asphalt.

culture.text: Trinidad's Carnival is one of the world's great street festivals. The steelpan, made from oil drums, was invented in Trinidad in the 1930s and 40s, and calypso and soca music began there. The writer V. S. Naipaul, who won the Nobel Prize in 2001, was born in Trinidad.

items.title: Steelpan
items.text: The only acoustic instrument invented in the 1900s, made from oil drums.

items.title: Carnival
items.text: Two days of costumed parades before Lent.

sport.text: Cricket and football are the most popular sports. Brian Lara, from Trinidad, set records for the highest scores in Test and first-class cricket. Keshorn Walcott won the javelin at the 2012 Olympics, and the country qualified for the 2006 World Cup.
